judge.copies_example: Fig. 4 caption: "Superconducting quantum interference patterns for Dev 1 (a), and Dev 2 (b) ... exhibiting clear SQUID-like oscillations"; Fig. 5b (Dev 3) "showing behavior similar to that in Fig. 4".
judge.orig_phrase: orig-r1: "three independent devices suggests that our results originate from intrinsic properties of ZrTe5" and "This facet selectivity is robust across multiple devices and two different superconductors"; orig-r2: "First, SQUID-like patterns appear for two separate Al/ZrTe5 devices."
judge.cut_evidence: Notes: "The extracted text looks incomplete in three places": p. 7 "announces 'the following three observations' and then starts at 'Second'", plus double spaces on p. 2 and p. 8 (the other two cut sites); report question 5 asks "What is the first, and which figure carries it?" Test marks unchanged (part/no/part).
judge.verdict: Registered: it located all three cut sites and asked for the missing first observation, blaming text extraction rather than a test, while the marks stayed the same because the device count survives in the figure captions.

judge.orig_phrase: orig-r1: "The text says the reconstruction is limited by the field range (p. 7)"; orig-r2 quotes "the finite magnetic-field range of the measured interference pattern" (p. 7).
judge.cut_evidence: Lookalike not used in any run; cut run asks "Which field window and resolution went into the Js(x) profiles of Fig. 4d,e, and do the two peaks hold if the window is narrowed?" without saying text is missing (orig-r2 asked a similar field-range question).
judge.verdict: Not registered: the question about the reconstruction window is one the originals also raised, and nothing points to the missing upper-bound caveat or Fig. S7.

judge.copies_example: SI heading "High field SC in the semiclassical regime of a non-moiré ballistic graphene JJ" and Fig. S15 caption "high-field superconductivity in a non-moiré ballistic graphene JJ" remain, but the 2rc = L reading of Fig. S15d is gone.
judge.orig_phrase: orig-r2: "A non-aligned graphene junction stays below 2rc = L (Fig. S15d)."; orig-r1: "well beyond the 2rc = L limit that bounds them in the main Dirac band and in a non-moiré control junction (Fig. S15)".
judge.cut_evidence: Targeted marks identical to both originals (part, all); the non-aligned junction is cited only for Fabry-Pérot ("non-aligned graphene junction (S15)"), with no request for a trivial-junction high-field comparison.
judge.verdict: Not registered: the run quietly stopped using the non-moiré control as a 2rc = L comparison, and no mark changed and no question was asked.

judge.copies_example: "Table S1 summarizes the main geometrical parameters of the four devices presented in this work" and SI "High-field superconductivity in a second device GH2".
judge.orig_phrase: orig-r1 and orig-r2 both quote "No high field superconductivity nor clear Fabry-Pérot oscillations were observed for the other two devices GH3 and GH4."; orig-r2 also quotes "reproduced across multiple additional devices" (p. 3).
judge.cut_evidence: Notes: "GH3 and GH4 appear only at zero field"; questions ask "Were GH3 and GH4 taken above 1 T?" and "If GH3 and GH4 showed no pockets, or weren't measured, could the SI say so?". Test marks unchanged (part/no/all).
judge.verdict: Partly registered: it asked directly for the cut GH3/GH4 high-field outcome, but read it as something the paper never said, not as missing text, and the marks did not move.

judge.copies_example: SI p. 22: "Our criteria is to define Ic as the I value at which dV /dI reaches 50% of the RN"; Fig. 3 caption "superconductivity (high conductance 1/R)".
judge.orig_phrase: orig-r2 quotes "we use the base-temperature zero-bias conductance 1/R as a proxy for the onset of the superconducting phase" (p. 7).
judge.cut_evidence: The lookalike was skipped ("no automated pass/fail protocol"), as in orig-r2; the Ic rule was taken from the SI copy ("Ic is defined at 50% of RN"); its 20 mS cutoff question matches orig-r1's.
judge.verdict: Not registered, and there was little to register: the Ic rule survives in the SI and the run used that copy.

judge.orig_phrase: orig-r1 and orig-r2 both quote "Other trivial mechanisms for the zero-field SDE (e.g., self-fields, Meissner screening, and geometric asymmetry) are ruled out, as shown in SM [40]." (p. 4).
judge.cut_evidence: Marks identical (no, part); it quoted the intro instead, and notes say "The paper names the mechanism in the introduction but does not argue against it for its own devices", with no suggestion that text is missing. Its bare-NbSe2 question matches orig-r2's.
judge.verdict: Not registered as a deletion: it described the cut paper accurately as not arguing against screening, but no mark or question changed.

judge.orig_phrase: orig-r1 and orig-r2 both quote "Similar behavior is also observed in another device #2, as shown in Supplementary Material (SM) [40]." (p. 2).
judge.cut_evidence: Notes: "Devices #1 and #3 are shown; device #2 is never mentioned"; question 2: "Why were the others set aside, including device #2 if it was measured?". Test marks unchanged (part/no/part).
judge.verdict: Registered by inference: the gap in device numbering made it ask about the cut device #2, though it did not suspect missing text and the marks stayed the same.

judge.cut_evidence: No run used the lookalike; the cut run never mentions sign conventions, and its remanent-field questions match the originals'.
judge.verdict: Not registered, but neither original relied on the sign-convention sentence either, so nothing was lost.

judge.copies_example: Only the tuning half survives ("magnetic field and the lateral size of Bi2Te3 islands, we further realize controllable ..."); "all measured vortices" appears nowhere else.
judge.orig_phrase: orig-r1 and orig-r2 both quote "MZMs are observed in all measured vortices" (Abstract).
judge.cut_evidence: Test "Devices and datasets measured, and how many showed the effect" dropped from part (both originals) to no, and the report-counts check from "partly" to "Not done"; there is no remark about missing text.
judge.verdict: Registered as a lower mark only: the counts test fell from part to no, consistent with the claim being absent, without the run noticing a gap.

judge.orig_phrase: orig-r1 and orig-r2 quote "To minimize possible defect-related effects, we performed the measurements in a defect-free region" ('Anisotropic Abrikosov vortex').
judge.cut_evidence: Lookalike unused in the originals and in the cut run; the cut run asks "does the core sit on an interstitial Fe or other defect in topography?" and says "Impurity states at the core aren't checked"; fine-tuning "how chosen" also fell to no.
judge.verdict: Weakly registered: it asked whether the core sits on a defect, which the cut sentence would have answered, but it did not notice a gap.

judge.copies_example: Main text: "two pairs of low-energy symmetric peaks appear near the zero energy, with an energy spacing of about 0.7 meV, suggestive of integer quantized CdGM states"; Fig. 3G caption "Statistical analysis of the peak positions in vortex core" (fitted values gone).
judge.orig_phrase: orig-r1: "we extract five discrete states ... which approximately follow an integer quantized sequence (Fig. 3G)"; orig-r2: "we extract five discrete states ... from the spectra by multi-peak fitting".
judge.cut_evidence: Lookalike used only in orig-r1, so no lower-than-both; the cut run asks "how well does a half-odd-integer sequence ... fit the peak positions in Fig. 3G, compared with the integer sequence?" (orig-r1 asked a similar fit request).
judge.verdict: Not really registered: it fell back on the surviving 0.7 meV sentence and asked for a fit the originals also wanted, with no sign it saw the fitted levels were missing.

judge.orig_phrase: orig-r1 and orig-r2 quote "The chains were constructed in defect-free regions" (p. 2) under fine-tuning-and-selection.
judge.cut_evidence: Targeted marks identical (part, part, no); only the non-targeted fine-tuning test "How the shown data were chosen" fell from part to no; no question about defects near the chains.
judge.verdict: Not registered for the targeted lookalike; the cut shows up only as a lower fine-tuning mark.

judge.copies_example: Fig. 4(d) caption: "Calculated zero-energy LDOS including a weak linear variation of the local exchange coupling J"; Fig. S1(e): "linear accumulative perturbation of 1%".
judge.orig_phrase: orig-r1: "a small variation of the local coupling to the superconducting substrate is sufficient to account for the measured asymmetry"; orig-r2: "the interaction will be local and will keep the topology of the perfect chain" (p. S4).
judge.cut_evidence: one-end-only stays "ruled out" (all, no) as in both originals; the run rebuilt the explanation from the surviving captions ("The theory reproduces this only with a linear J variation (Fig. 4d)").
judge.verdict: Not registered: the captions left enough of the J-variation model that the run did not miss the cut explanation.

judge.orig_phrase: orig-r1: "we subtract the dI/dV of the pristine surface from the middle of the chain dI/dV" (p. S4); orig-r2: Fig. S3 "curve after subtracting 'the dI/dV of the pristine surface'".
judge.cut_evidence: No run used the lookalike; the cut run never mentions subtraction, cites only "The red curve is the full conductance", and notes "how the ±50 µeV was set not stated"; the report-processing check fell to "Not done".
judge.verdict: Not registered: the run dropped all mention of the background subtraction without flagging its absence.

judge.copies_example: Fig. S3 caption (device C) survives: "c, f, i, End-to-end correlation analysis using the product of the the third derivative at zero bias ... l, Relative fraction of gate voltages exhibiting correlated zero-bias conductance peaks"; the device B outcome ("no clear distinction", "majority of the time") is gone.
judge.orig_phrase: orig-r1 and orig-r2: "We find that both regimes contain ZBPs on either end (see Fig. 4c,f,i,l) the majority of the time." (abs-quantum-dot row); orig-r1 check 3: "we evaluated the end-to-end correlation using the relative signs of the third derivative".
judge.cut_evidence: Notes: "the main-text paragraph on end-to-end correlation stops after 'significant overlap in our devices.' and its outcome is missing" and "the Fig. 4 caption stops after panel k"; one-end-only marks unchanged (part, part).
judge.verdict: Registered: the notes pinpoint the missing correlation outcome and Fig. 4 caption, though it blames the extraction and leaves the one-end-only marks unchanged.

judge.orig_phrase: orig-r2 local-probe row: "the boundary modes should be localised at the junctions without significant overlap in our devices."; orig-r1 exceptional-point row: "we estimate the experimental localisation length of the MBSs to be a few 100 nm".
judge.cut_evidence: Local-probe-loophole stays "Tested in part" (part, no), as in both originals; the only trace is the exceptional-point note shifting from "argued, not tested" (orig-r1) to "data bear on it", with no mention of a missing estimate.
judge.verdict: Not registered: the run quietly dropped the localisation-length argument and neither flagged a gap nor changed the targeted marks.

judge.copies_example: p. 5 still says "The fact this occurs even in theoretically trivial regions suggests that at least some of these ZBPs are driven by disorder effects" and "both showing a large number of ZBPs at both ends"; Fig. S3 caption keeps "at zero magnetic field".
judge.orig_phrase: orig-r1: "we observe these even in theoretically trivial windows and notably even at zero Bx" and "we do not see a significant difference between the VG dependence of ZBPs"; orig-r2: "the zero field ZBPs largely have a strong dependence on VG (Fig. 4a-b)".
judge.cut_evidence: Notes: "Several stretches of the extracted text have blank gaps (after the abstract's 'align with these global features.' and after '(see Fig. 3b-c).' on p. 5), so some text may be missing", which are the two cut sites; disorder-induced-zbp marks unchanged (part, part, all).
judge.verdict: Registered as a possible gap at the exact cut sites, attributed to extraction, with no change to the targeted lookalike's marks (the Kondo row lost its quote and reads "Not discussed").

judge.copies_example: Supplement S1.E (device C): "However, not all features can be associated with critical-current anomalies. In particular, additional spectral jumps occur at large magnetic fields."
judge.orig_phrase: orig-r1 and orig-r2 trivial-Andreev-band row: "there are also nonlocal conductance jumps at Bx values that do not correspond to the Ic features, especially at large values of magnetic flux."
judge.cut_evidence: Trivial-andreev-band row keeps "Tested in part" (no, part) and swaps in a Suppl. p. 6 quote on gate sign changes; no gap noticed or specific request for the mismatch.
judge.verdict: Not registered: the run substituted another quote and kept identical marks.

judge.orig_phrase: orig-r1 and orig-r2 check 6: "The line resistances required were determined from two-terminal resistance measurements of the cryostat lines." (Supp. p. 2)
judge.cut_evidence: Report check 6 drops to "Not done" (both originals "Partly") because Supplement Section C "has a heading and no text"; question 5 asks how the series and line resistances were calibrated and whether the Martinez et al. correction was applied.
judge.verdict: Clearly registered: it named the empty Section C, lowered the raw-conductance check and asked for exactly the cut calibration (the lookalike itself was skipped in all runs).

judge.copies_example: Supplement keeps "Applying the ν = −1 reference periods to our ν = −4/3 data yields results consistent with both p = 4 and charge e/3."; the numbers 0.37 ± 0.04, 3.47 ± 0.79 and the top-gate ratio 2.9 ± 0.6 are gone.
judge.orig_phrase: Reports rely only on surviving text (orig-r1: "Your ν = −4/3 and ν = −1 checks at 14 T support the transfer"; orig-r2: "ADG versus TG only at ν = −1 and −4/3, Fig. S5"); the cut numbers appear only in both notes ("−4/3 gives 0.37 ± 0.04").
judge.cut_evidence: charge-regime-map drops to "Partly" (both originals "Done"), but the stated reasons are the missing slope sign and the unreliable ν = 2/3 FFT, not the calibration; coulomb row marks (part, part) equal orig-r1.
judge.verdict: Not registered in substance: one check went lower for unrelated reasons, and the missing ADG benchmark was neither noticed nor asked for.

judge.copies_example: Fig. S10 caption: "the histogram method and 2D-FFT analysis agree"; Supplement K gives "∆B = 19.6 ± 4 mT" from the repeated-sweep histograms.
judge.orig_phrase: Reports cite only the surviving Fig. S13 ("Raw data from 20 consecutive repetitions of the same measurement"); the histogram cross-check appears only in orig-r2 notes.
judge.cut_evidence: Charge-trap row (all, no, part) matches orig-r2 and beats orig-r1, charge-repeat-sweeps stays "Partly", and the notes still record "histogram ∆B = 19.6 ± 4 mT" from the surviving supplement.
judge.verdict: Not registered, and there was little to register: the histogram evidence survives in the supplement and the run used it.

judge.copies_example: p. 8 still says the doubled regime appears 'but not at the conventional odd-denominator FQH states ν = −1/3 and −4/3' and 'Even at the largest side-gate voltage accessible in our device, no period doubling is observed'; Supp. H heading 'Absence of doubling at ν = −4/3' and the Fig. S6 panel line '0.2 V, 2 V, and 5 V' and the full Fig. S7 caption ('No doubling of the gate voltage periodicity is observed') remain.
judge.orig_phrase: Neither report.md nor flags.json quotes a cut span; for 'Shifts absent' orig-r1 cites 'ν = −2 gate-voltage periodicity is consistent with electron charge' and orig-r2 cites ν = −1 and −2 (Fig. S4). Only the notes lean on it (orig-r1 notes: 'none at −4/3, −1/3 ... 5 V max used').
judge.cut_evidence: Notes say 'p. 6: the sentence "the ADG period doubles ... at ν = −5/2, −1/2, 2/3 and 3/2" is followed by a gap in the extracted text, so text may be missing' (the exact cut site), but the charge-trap row is unchanged ('Shifts absent ...: all', status 'tested in part', same as both originals) and the report does not raise it.
judge.verdict: Partly: the run spotted the textual gap at one cut site and put it down to extraction, but it did not register any loss of evidence because the odd-denominator null result survives elsewhere, and its charge-trap marks did not move.

judge.copies_example: Sweep part only: the Fig. S4 panels still carry 'Sweep #1' to 'Sweep #6' with 'η = 17.07%', 'η = -30.86%', 'η = -14.07%', and p. 5 keeps 'between −30.86% and 17.07% (Figs. S3 to S5)'. The per-stage oxidation sweep counts and the whole Hc1 / vortex-entry estimate ('0.59 T', '19.6 nm', 'vortex') have no copy left.
judge.orig_phrase: orig-r1 and orig-r2 both quote 'only the second exhibited a field-free SDE, corresponding to Fig. 2(c) in the main text' (Supp. p. 2) in the fine-tuning row; orig-r2's vortex row quotes 'ordinary vortex entry into the superconducting layer is not expected under the in-plane training condition' (Fig. S10 caption).
judge.cut_evidence: For fine-tuning, 'How the shown data were chosen' drops from 'part' in both originals to 'no', and question 4 asks 'what do repeated sweeps of Device 11 at the second oxidation step look like, and how was the sweep with η = 83.61% (Fig. 2c) chosen?', which is exactly what the cut passage said. The run never says text is missing, and diode-vortex-screening stays at part/part.
judge.verdict: Registered the sweep-selection cut (lower mark plus a targeted request for the missing sweeps) but not the vortex-entry estimate, whose loss left the diode-vortex-screening row unchanged.

judge.copies_example: The evidence the argument used is still there: 'nonlinear magnetotransport measurements at 5 K using a reference CuMnAs bar without a superconducting Al layer ... without invoking superconducting transport' (p. 4 to 5) and the SQUID bound '(3×10−3 µB /Mn)' with 'The vanishingly small net mag-netization'. The wording that rules out flux trapping, vortex dynamics and stray fields ('spurious flux trapping', 'disfavors a stray-field mechanism') is gone.
judge.orig_phrase: orig-r1 quotes 'the anisotropic remanence itself originates in CuMnAs rather than from spurious flux trapping or vortex dynamics, both known to generate SDE28,29' and 'this also disfavors a stray-field mechanism associated with uncompensated magnetization30'; orig-r2 quotes both, the first one in its diode-vortex-screening row.
judge.cut_evidence: diode-vortex-screening goes to 'not tested' (data bear on it) with tests no/no, against 'tested in part' with no/part in both originals. The run gives no sign of seeing a gap. micromagnet-stray-field is used only in the cut run (the originals had outside stray-field rows, also 'tested in part'), so there is nothing to compare it with.
judge.verdict: Registered it only indirectly: the vortex-screening status dropped once the authors' argument was gone, but the run did not notice or ask about the missing passage, and the stray-field reading was unchanged.
judge.session_override: Changed from 'lowered' by the session after checking: d1-r1/notes.md line 87 says references 28 to 30 are listed but not cited and 'Either a passage was lost in extraction or the citations are elsewhere.' The cut removed the passage that cited them. The status also dropped (tested in part to not tested).

numeric.change: gate period 56 to 63 mV to 112 to 126 mV
